issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting guidance about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section (lines 69-71) instructs initializing attributes (including stock) in the SealSaloon constructor, while a later section (lines 77-81) explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing an instance field in a constructor and requiring it to be static are contradictory and could confuse students about whether stock should be an instance or a class-level field and where it should be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: decide whether stock is a static (class-level) attribute or an instance attribute. If stock must be shared across all SealSaloon instances, state that it should be declared static (and can be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer). If it should be an instance final field, remove the requirement that it be static and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor. Update the problem statement so the instruction about initialization location and the static requirement are consistent.
